home.hero.title: What can satellite data really tell us about change across the Congo Basin?
home.hero.lead: Pick a place and a clue. See the record from NASA data, then check whether the trend holds up to a statistical test.
home.questions.title: Three questions to start with
home.q1.title: Are afternoons getting hotter in Yaoundé?
home.q2.title: Is the air getting drier?
home.q3.title: Is rainfall changing?
home.map.title: Eleven locations, one clue at a time
home.map.note: Each point is one NASA POWER grid cell (~55 × 70 km), not a city boundary. Eleven points are not a basin-wide average.
home.map.alt: Map of Central Africa with the outline of the Congo River basin and {n} locations coloured by level of evidence for {variable}, {period}. Yaoundé is drawn as a hollow marker: it lies outside the hydrological basin. The same results are listed in the table below.

home.pnote: A small p-value means the observed trend would be unusual if there were no underlying trend.
